e1_claim_level_secondary.caveat:
Claim-level labelling marks a claim as a gap when its single lexical best-match
element was mutated. Measured on this corpus, 141 of 161 such claims remain
genuinely implemented by other elements, so this table understates every
evidence-based policy and is retained only as a diagnostic.

e3_identifier_ablation.note:
Identifier ablation renames the given fraction of defined function and class
names to opaque tokens. File paths and docstrings are left alone, so the NAME
channel can still fire on the path and DOC is untouched. NAME is one of the
seven evidence channels, so ablating it removes evidence the method genuinely
uses; a fall in cdc separation across the sweep is a real cost, not an artefact.
